chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: When you wash your deceased, be gentle with him, do not wring him, do not press any joint of his, and do not bring any of the camphor near his ears. Then take his turban and spread it folded over his head, cast its two ends behind him, and leave his forehead uncovered.
I said: And the hanut, how should I apply it? He said: It is placed in his nostrils, on the places of his sajdah, and on his joints.

I said: Then the shroud? He said: You take a piece of cloth and tie his lower part with it, drawing his thighs together with it so that what is there may be kept enclosed; and what is made from cotton is better. Then he is shrouded with a qamis, a wrapping cloth, and a burd in which the shroud is gathered.

key_terms.بِقَمِيصٍ: a shirt-like garment used as part of the shroud
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a piece of cloth used to bind the lower part of the body
key_terms.لِفَافَةٍ: a wrapping cloth forming part of the shroud
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِهِ: the places of prostration on the body where hanut is applied
key_terms.ٱلْحَنُوطُ: the perfuming substance applied to specific parts of the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed, perfumed, and shrouded according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the manner of washing and shrouding the deceased with care and gentleness. It specifies aspects of applying camphor and hanut, arranging the head covering, and preparing the kafan, making it a jurisprudential text on funerary rites.
